case_assessment.summary: The graph captures the main dust-explosion chain reasonably well: combustible phenolic resin dust was dispersed near line 405 and ignited, producing the dust explosion. The main weaknesses are on the ignition side of the sequence, where the graph omits the explicitly documented oven temperature-controller malfunction/manual open-door operation, and in a few weak or overly generic edges. There is also a schema-compliance issue because the H1 evidence is paraphrased rather than verbatim.
main_problems: The ignition pathway is under-specified because the documented line 405 oven controller malfunction/manual open-door operation is missing.
The line 405 baghouse mechanical-failure node is too generic relative to the more immediate plugged transition/loss-of-suction condition described in the report.
Some edges are weak or overly transitive, especially C2 -> Ev3 and C1 -> C6.
H1 evidence is not a direct quote and should be replaced with verbatim report language.

node_updates.current_state: Evidence is a paraphrased summary beginning with "The Executive Summary states..." rather than a verbatim quote.
node_updates.suggested_state: "A February 20, 2003, dust explosion at the CTA Acoustics, Inc. facility in Corbin, Kentucky, killed seven and injured 37 workers." and/or "combustible phenolic resin dust that had accumulated throughout the facility fueled the explosion."
node_updates.reason: The schema requires direct quoted evidence from the incident description. The current evidence text is not verbatim.
node_updates.evidence: "A February 20, 2003, dust explosion at the CTA Acoustics, Inc. facility in Corbin, Kentucky, killed seven and injured 37 workers."

node_updates.current_state: Name: Poor functioning of line 405 baghouse
node_updates.suggested_state: Name: Line 405 baghouse/transition blockage and loss of suction
node_updates.reason: The immediate abnormal equipment condition linked to the cleaning blowdown was not just generic poor performance; the report directly describes a plugged transition, clogged bags, and lack of suction. Renaming makes the causal link to Ev1 more precise.
node_updates.evidence: "the transition leading to the baghouse was plugged." and "the poor functioning of the baghouse and resulting lack of suction in the mat-former caused excessive release of dust from the production line."

node_additions.reason: A key pre-ignition step is missing. The report documents a temperature-controller malfunction that forced manual operation with oven access doors being opened and closed. This abnormal oven condition is directly relevant to the ignition pathway and is explicitly identified as a contributing cause.
node_additions.evidence: "the temperature controller was no longer regulating the oven temperature so controls were switched to manual by the line operators." and "The oven temperature was then controlled by opening and closing the access doors on the east and west sides of the oven."

edge_deletions.reason: This edge is too generic. The report supports a more specific ignition-enabling path through the malfunctioning temperature controller/manual open-door oven operation, rather than from high temperature alone directly to the unknown ignition source.
edge_deletions.evidence: "Operating the oven with malfunctioning temperature control equipment and open doors was a nonroutine situation" and "Flames may have escaped through an open oven door, or the dust cloud may have entered the oven and ignited."

edge_deletions.reason: This edge is overly generic and weak. The report attributes dispersion to cleaning and blowdown activities, not to the solid phase condition itself. Keeping it overstates a transitive relationship.
edge_deletions.evidence: "these activities and other line-cleaning tasks—such as blowing out pipes with compressed air and dry sweeping floors—generated a cloud of combustible dust around line 405."

issues_summary.description: The graph omits the documented line 405 oven temperature-controller malfunction/manual open-door operation that materially strengthens the ignition pathway.
The edge C2 -> Ev3 is too generic; the report supports a more specific intermediate step tied to controller malfunction and open oven doors.
The edge C1 -> C6 is overly transitive because dust dispersion is directly tied to cleaning/blowdown activities rather than solid phase alone.
H1 evidence is paraphrased instead of being a direct quote from the report.
Ev2 is named too generically; the report more specifically describes clogging/blockage and loss of suction in the line 405 baghouse system.
